summary: A deer longs for streams, and the speaker longs for God in the same way. Joel describes the animals’ longing when fire has consumed the pasture and the streams have dried up. A related spelling names a garden bed.

senses.definition: The comparison moves from a thirsty animal to the psalmist asking when he will again appear before God. Joel sets the animals’ longing alongside the drying up of the streams.
The vine sends out roots for water from the bed where it was planted. The lover goes down into a garden among the beds of spices.

note: The relationship between a planted bed and longing remains uncertain. Lane’s Arabic عرج describes ascending or limping, and gives no direct support for longing. The name Arad ends in daleth.
